title: Virtualization for Large Lists
description: Render thousands of rows efficiently using virtualization libraries and native techniques.

blocks.text: Rendering a list of thousands of items creates thousands of DOM nodes. Even if each item is lightweight, the browser struggles with layout, paint, and memory. Virtualization solves this by rendering only the items visible in the viewport plus a small overscan.

blocks.caption: Virtualization renders only visible items

blocks.title: Considerations
items: Fixed-height virtualization is simpler and faster because row positions are calculated mathematically
Variable-height virtualization measures items dynamically, which is more flexible but computationally heavier
Choose fixed-height when possible, especially for tables, log viewers, and chat messages

blocks.text: react-window is a lightweight, widely used virtualization library. It provides FixedSizeList and VariableSizeList components.

blocks.title: Virtualizing a Large Table
blocks.content: Render 10,000 rows without freezing the browser.

blocks.title: Provide a Stable Key
blocks.text: Always provide a stable key prop for each row. react-window reuses DOM elements aggressively. If your key changes, virtualization breaks and React will lose track of item state.
react-virtuoso is a modern alternative with first-class support for variable-height items, grouped lists, and smooth scrolling. It automatically measures item heights and handles dynamic content.

blocks.title: Variable-Height List with Virtuoso
blocks.content: Virtuoso handles dynamic heights out of the box.

blocks.text: Overscan renders a small buffer of items above and below the viewport. This reduces blank space during fast scrolling but increases DOM nodes. Tune overscan based on item complexity and scroll speed.

Virtualization is most effective when you have more than a few hundred items or when each item contains complex content. For smaller lists, the added complexity is not worth it. Always test scroll performance with realistic data sizes.

items.text: Use a stable key based on item ID
items.hint: Avoid array index as key for large dynamic lists
Memoize inner items if they have their own state

items.text: Set a fixed height if items are uniform
items.hint: Fixed height yields the best scroll performance

items.text: Profile scroll performance with React DevTools
items.hint: Check frame rate during fast scrolling

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
points: Virtualization renders only visible items plus overscan
react-window is lightweight and ideal for fixed-height lists
react-virtuoso supports variable heights and grouped lists
Stable keys are critical for virtualization to work correctly
Use virtualization for lists larger than a few hundred items
